title: The view from the top
hook: from here you can see every path and the one direction they face
tomorrow: Jordan drives Amira to the airport. what did her grandma tell her?

segments.voice: Yesterday, gratitude for everything: a forehead lowered for the good and the hard alike. All praise. Today, you lift your head and look around.

The night before you leave home is always the same: a suitcase that won't zip, a charger you can't find, a family group chat that's about to get busier. Everyone is about to be somewhere different. A dad at his coffee shop, a grandmother on her couch, a little cousin at school, a best friend at a college three hours away. Scattered across a map. And yet, from high enough up, there's one thing they all still do the same way.
screen: `A SUITCASE THAT WON'T ZIP.` → `SCATTERED ACROSS A MAP.` → `ONE THING THEY ALL DO THE SAME.`

segments.voice: They face the same way. The qibla is the direction of prayer, toward the Ka'ba in Mecca. In every mosque, a niche in the wall, the mihrab, points to it. From a kitchen in Houston, it's one angle. From a dorm in Chicago, a slightly different one. Zoom out far enough and the rows of people praying across the world all turn toward a single point. Here's the picture to tell a friend tonight: around the Ka'ba itself, the rows can't all face one wall, so they become circles, people praying toward the center, facing one another across it. That's the view from the top. Every path visible, and every path turned one way. The Qur'an widens it further: "Unto Allah belong the East and the West, and whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah's Countenance." The qibla gathers the body; God isn't confined to it. And then it widens it again, to everyone: "O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another." One human family, made different on purpose, so the knowing would be worth doing. For someone about to scatter, that's what this path gives. Not a promise that everyone stays in one house. A direction everyone shares, wherever the suitcase ends up, and a reason to know the people from the other tribes along the way.
screen: `THE QIBLA: ONE DIRECTION.` · `RINGS AROUND THE KA'BA.` · `WHEREVER YOU TURN.` · `NATIONS AND TRIBES, TO KNOW ONE ANOTHER.` · then, large: `EVERYTHING FACES HIM.`

segments.voice: Find a window or a doorway and look out, as far as you can see. Let one person come to mind behind each roof or road you can see, people you know and people you don't. Then turn toward the qibla if you know it, or simply stay where you are, and sit and look until the time is up.
screen: `LOOK AS FAR AS YOU CAN SEE.` · `A PERSON BEHIND EACH ROOF.` · `SIT AND LOOK.`

segments.voice: The view from the top: every path in sight, and the one direction they all face.
screen: `THE VIEW FROM THE TOP — today's word`.

segments.voice: Something to keep: everything faces him, even a family scattered across a map. Fourteen of fifteen, one step left.

screen: `DAY 1790 COUNTS.` → `THE SUMMIT · 14 OF 15.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DID JORDAN'S GRANDMA TELL HER?`

howItsDone: Muslims everywhere face the qibla, toward the Ka'ba in Mecca, when they pray; mosques mark it with a mihrab, and travelers find it with a compass or a phone.

fork.setup: on a road trip, your phone dies at prayer time in a rest-stop parking lot, and you can't find the qibla. what fits today?

fork.reveal: 2:115: unto Allah belong the East and the West. you do your honest best with the direction, and the prayer goes on.
